To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the maximum entropy technique is useful for synthesizing an initial beam distribution function from a set of slit scans, (b) the synthesized beam distributions yield better agreement with the reference case than the simple model distribution, (c) the emittance evolution in the simulation is sensitive to the initial conditions and the initial distribution function, and (d) the maximum entropy method can be applied to optical slit data, and the resulting distributions are consistent with those from the Faraday cup slit data

(1) simulations of HCX using initial conditions synthesized from experimental slit-scan diagnostics exhibit emittance growth and beam halo formation in qualitative agreement with experimental observations, and (2) the use of slit-scan data to initialize simulations has been shown to be feasible, and the results are promising.

(1) initial beam distributions synthesized from experimental slit scan data can be used to launch HCX-type 2D particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations, (2) the resulting simulations exhibit emittance evolution similar that of the reference HCX simulation, and (3) this approach can be extended to 4D PIC simulations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of techniques for simulating intense beam transport, and for extracting information about the beam's 6D distribution function.
the application of maximum-entropy methods to the problem of reconstructing the 4D particle distribution function from 2D slit scan diagnostics.
the development of methods for simulating the dynamics of intense particle beams, using initial conditions synthesized from experimental data.

the simulation of the HCX beam is still a work in progress.
the HCX beam dynamics is not yet understood.
the HCX beam dynamics is well described by the 2D model, but that a 3D model would be needed to describe the HCX beam in the context of the HCX experiment.

the use of the maximum-entropy Monte Carlo method for the reconstruction of the beam distribution is an important step forward in the simulation of intense ion beam propagation.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the 4D beam distributions synthesized from slit-sweep data are a useful starting point for simulations, and the techniques we use to synthesize them are robust.
the 4D beam distribution is a critical element in the beam evolution.
the 2D projections are not sufficient to uniquely specify the 3D distribution, and that the 4D information is necessary to obtain the correct evolution of emittance and other parameters.
